newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan not surprised by alleged China donations.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan not surprised by alleged China donations.

text.p: Taiwan, which last year was accused of illegal contributions to U.S. President Bill Clinton's re-election campaign, said on Friday it was not surprised by a similar allegation against rival China.
"Under the kind of system of the Chinese communists, I am not a bit surprised that it would have done that kind of thing," Foreign Ministry spokesman Peter Cheng told reporters.

The Washington Post reported on Thursday that a Justice Department probe into improper political fund-raising activities had uncovered evidence that the Chinese Embassy was involved in funnelling contributions to the Democratic National Committee.
"Under their system, they will not be subjected to any supervision by any agencies," Cheng added.

The Post said its sources declined to provide details about the scope of the evidence on alleged donations by Chinese representatives. The sources declined to specify what foreign contributions might have been involved, but said the new evidence was serious.
State television quoted Cheng as saying the Taiwan government did not make improper political contributions to the Clinton campaign.
Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party denied in October 1996 media reports that it was willing to donate US$15 million to Clinton's re-election campaign.
Taiwan and China have been rivals since a civil war split them in 1949. Beijing has regarded the island as a renegade province ineligible for international diplomatic ties.
